findings.text: follow-on: _CREDENTIAL_MARKERS contains the bare token 'denied', matched as a substring and checked before _UNREACHABLE_MARKERS (line 198), so a transport failure whose message carries that substring is misclassified as a decisive credential error. Reproduced: fetch_layer(..., runner=<stderr 'dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: connect: permission denied'>) raises LayerRegistryCredentialError where the layer state is in fact unknown (the case LayerRegistryUnreachable exists for). Impact: a validator run behind a restrictive egress firewall would fail hard instead of skipping - the skip-vs-fail inversion this rung was written to fix, reintroduced on a narrower input.

justifications.durability: The new guard is genuine and I falsified it: removing the credential classification turns the credential cases red (3 failed, EXIT=1, reproduced). Deficiencies: the credential markers are matched as bare substrings and checked before the transport markers, and the marker 'denied' is broad enough to capture the substring in a transport-layer failure. Reproduced: fetch_layer with stderr 'dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: connect: permission denied' raises LayerRegistryCredentialError, not LayerRegistryUnreachable, so a sandbox or firewall that refuses egress (state genuinely unknown) is now a decisive, non-skippable failure rather than a clean skip - the exact inversion the rung exists to prevent. The unknown-digest path is unaffected (test_an_unknown_digest_is_a_fetch_error_not_a_skip passes).
justifications.evidence: Reproduced independently in a scratch tree extracted from the reviewed head (git archive 7c7fe7e0 -> $TMPDIR/review-head): the gate run as a fresh process gives 10 passed, 0 skipped, EXIT=0, matching the reviewed manifest's headline (layer-fetch-gate.log, revision line ee71c73e). The declared negative control reproduces as an independent red arm: disabling the credential branch (if False and any(... _CREDENTIAL_MARKERS)) turns the three credential ids red at EXIT=1, exactly the ids the reviewed negative-control.log names. Gaps: the reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm, so the designed base-vs-head delta reads no base log; and its cited layer-fetch-gate.log header names revision ee71c73e (the base SHA) with a timestamp (07:19) two minutes before the commits (07:21). The gate therefore ran on the uncommitted working tree rather than a commit, so the header understates what the run measured.
justifications.fit: The change follows module idiom: LayerRegistryCredentialError joins its sibling error classes with a matching docstring, the marker tuples keep the comment explaining skip semantics (line 28-29), and _classify_failure keeps one return-per-classification shape. No plan, sprint or version label appears in the code or comment. The test file keeps its section-comment structure and splits the credential cases into a parametrised test rather than expanding an existing one.
justifications.goal_fidelity: plan s3 (the availability gate must distinguish registry authentication failure from registry unavailability; the pinned case record carries each case's layer digests) is answered exactly: nova/database/layer_fetch.py:60 adds LayerRegistryCredentialError, and _classify_failure (line 198) tests the credential markers before the transport markers, so an authorization or token failure raises a decisive LayerFetchError that a validator's LayerRegistryUnreachable skip cannot swallow; tests/test_layer_fetch.py:172 asserts the credential cases are not LayerRegistryUnreachable, and test_every_pinned_layer_is_fetched_and_verified (line 58) now fetches all 8 pinned layers (analytic input/machine_description, CORSICA, DINA, ASTRA input/reference) instead of the analytic pair alone, verifying each against its pinned digest and size. This retires both open items the publish-entry landing comment named: 'authentication faults are classified as an unreachable registry, and the six ITER digests are checked only for form'.
justifications.reuse: The change reuses the existing machinery rather than adding any: the classifier it extends already existed, and fetch/verify/publish still route through nova/database/content_store.py publish_files, read_regular_bytes and verified_destination (imported at line 13-23) with no new public surface beyond the one error class. The digest-coverage test folds all 8 pinned layers into one looped gate instead of adding eight tests, and reuses the _RECORD already parsed from tests/data-manifest.json.
justifications.scope_discipline: The whole diff between base and head is two paths, nova/database/layer_fetch.py and tests/test_layer_fetch.py, both inside the reviewed manifest's declared write paths; no out-of-scope file is touched. The declared write paths also name an evidence fragment (docs/evidence/fragments/forward-profile-validator-set/fpv-fetch-credential-faults.html) and a figures directory that this credential/digest rung did neither need nor write.
